newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech stock market pioneer found dead aged 37.
newsitem.headline: Czech stock market pioneer found dead aged 37.

text.p: Michael Hobbs, a Californian who helped pioneer the post-Communist free market in the Czech Republic, was found dead in his apartment, police said Wednesday. He was 37.

A police spokesman said Hobbs, who was working closely with the Prague Stock Exchange on the creation of a Securities Exchange Commission, was found by colleagues in the bathtub of his company-owned flat last Thursday. He had been dead for about one week.

The spokesman said that there were no signs of violence but that an official cause of death had not been determined because medical examiners cannot perform an autopsy until relatives arrive from the United States.
Hobbs, a native of San Diego and graduate of Yale University, came to the former Czechoslovakia in 1991 to teach finance at Masaryk University in the city of Brno.

There he co-founded the Czech brokerage firm Atlantik Financni Trhy in 1993 along with his former students Daniel Gladis and Karel Bastl, setting up a thriving business alongside the country's massive post-Communist privatisation programme.
